{"id": "74156dd2-7695-4c00-a7cd-24bdbda466eb", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "EBS gp3 volumes let you modify IOPS (and throughput) independently of size, without detaching the volume. Here's how to do it with the AWS CLI:

**Modify IOPS on an existing gp3 volume:**

```bash
aws ec2 modify-volume \
  --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
  --iops 6000
```

You can combine IOPS, throughput, and size changes in a single call:

```bash
aws ec2 modify-volume \
  --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
  --volume-type gp3 \
  --size 200 \
  --iops 6000 \
  --throughput 500
```

**Check the status of the modification:**

```bash
aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications \
  --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
```

A few things worth knowing:
- gp3 baseline is 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s throughput at no extra cost; you can provision up to 16,000 IOPS and 1,000 MiB/s (higher ceilings apply only to volumes attached to Nitro instances that support it).
- The volume stays attached and in use during the modification — no downtime required, though the optimization phase can take time depending on the amount of change.
- There's a cooldown: you generally need to wait at least 6 hours between size/IOPS/throughput modifications on the same volume (or until the previous modification finishes optimizing, whichever is longer).

Want me to check the current IOPS/throughput configuration on one of your actual EBS volumes before you run this?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
